intent: Remove measured redundant large-binary verification overhead in the private rehearsal guard without reducing the actual HTTP/security acceptance matrix or raising resource budgets.

evidence.diagnosis: The private native() guard rehashes the same Caddy binary on each probe. The native timeout was not caused by exhausting the stage log; no model was called.

approaches.description: Retain a full binary SHA-256 scan on every HTTP probe, with no guard semantic change.
approaches.advantage: Preserves the current byte-verification boundary exactly.
approaches.disadvantage: The measured run still exceeds the fixed 90-second/20%-CPU unit budget. Do not simply repeat it, extend limits, or report partial acceptance as complete.

approaches.description: Use a descriptor-pinned, root-controlled, non-business-writable runtime under an independently verified read-only unit mount; retain full SHA-256 at critical boundaries and check ownership, permissions, descriptor/path identity and change metadata on every probe.
approaches.advantage: Keeps the existing separate RPC/HTTP probes and introduces no new service, protocol method, package installation, public port or production change.
approaches.disadvantage: This changes the invariant from per-probe full-byte hashing to a protected-runtime invariant between full-hash boundaries. It requires explicit approval and is not equivalent against a hostile privileged host writer.

nonGoals: Do not implement this proposal until the changed verification boundary is explicitly approved.
Do not change product LACK code, model routing, Agent configuration, credentials, grants, DNS, ports or Relay.
Do not execute another Linux unit, reuse an unused allocation, restart production or publish.
Do not batch away HTTP probes, remove negative cases, raise budgets, accept stale proofs or add unsafe fallbacks.
preconditionsThatMustBeProvedNotAssumed: The exact Caddy input still matches the existing pinned SHA-256 and maximum size.
The binary and its relevant path ancestry are canonical, non-symlinked and root-controlled; neither UID 996 nor unprivileged groups/other users can write or replace them under the accepted policy.
The nearest effective mount covering the binary inside the actual business unit is read-only, including protection against a more-specific writable mount.
The business process remains UID 996/GID 987 with zero effective capabilities, NoNewPrivileges and the existing network/resource isolation.
A retained descriptor and the current pathname refer to the same regular single-link file, with identical device/inode, size, nanosecond change/modification metadata, owner/group and permissions.

The trusted-host-administrator assumption is explicitly accepted. This fast path must not be represented as cryptographic protection against an administrator able to defeat the read-only/ownership/metadata assumptions.

proposedBoundary.scope: Private HTTP probe guard only; unknown or non-probe operations keep full verification by default.
perProbe: Revalidate the pinned descriptor and current path/ancestry identities and permissions.
Check the effective read-only mount and unchanged unprivileged/no-capability execution context.
Keep existing source inventory, source-content hashes, configuration, model-disable, client-empty-list, port and root/data-identity checks.
Reject any replacement, relink, writable exposure, identity drift or uncertain proof; do not silently re-anchor to a changed file.
fullByteVerification: Initial binding before any fixture operation.
Before every actual Caddy executable invocation, including validation and service start.
At candidate acceptance boundaries after the complete HTTP matrix and before any acceptance receipt.
At final verification boundaries required to accept cleanup/recovery; a failed check cannot prevent attempts to stop owned children and close owned descriptors.
proposedBoundary.digestHelper: Keep digestRegularFile itself unchanged: every real invocation reads and verifies the complete bounded input. Do not introduce a cached-digest shortcut inside it.
proposedBoundary.unsupportedPreconditions: Fail the preparation/guard explicitly. Do not change production ownership or mount policy, create a hidden runtime copy, add kernel features or silently fall back to an unverified fast path.

preservedAcceptance: All GET/HEAD main-domain asset checks, expected bytes and exact nosniff header checks.
All Agent-domain asset denials and POST/PATCH/DELETE asset denials.
All original REST, OAuth/MCP, listener, workspace/configuration and client-empty-list restrictions.
Source drift, file replacement, hash mismatch, cleanup, write-lock and late-write protection; do not drop assertions merely to fit the budget.
Original immutable module/source pins, updated only for explicitly changed private modules.
Original phase log maximum 256; separate request journal maximum 2064 records and 2097152 bytes.
requiredLocalRegressionBeforeAnyNewLinux: Retain existing streaming-hash correctness, complete-read-per-invocation, bounds and descriptor-cleanup regressions.

Add explicit fast-path rejection cases for wrong owner, writable owner ancestry, group/other write permission, symlink/hardlink, replaced inode, truncated/grown file, content mutation, restored mtime with changed ctime, writable/more-specific mount and missing mount proof.
Prove full hashes still occur at initial binding, each executable invocation and each acceptance fence; do not rely on static source substrings as semantic proof.
Preserve all original HTTP/security assertions and verify both acceptance surfaces.
Prove constructor/close failures release only owned descriptors/children and preserve original error identity and incomplete-evidence rejection.
Keep original serial/late-callback diagnostic isolation and file/byte caps.
Do not claim unchanged safety or native acceptance merely because older tests remain green.

futureNativeGate.required: After explicit local implementation approval and passing related regressions, submit a fresh bounded Linux scope and re-prove effective ownership/mount policy, full acceptance, actual timing and rollback. No production publication is implied.

decisionRequested: Approve approach B for bounded private local implementation and regression only, or retain approach A and accept that the current native acceptance remains blocked. The read-only/ownership preconditions and changed threat-model boundary must not be implicit.
